title: Reading your paycheck: gross pay, take-home pay and deductions

scenes.heading: Reading your paycheck
scenes.narration: Your first pay stub can be confusing. The amount you earn isn't the amount that lands in your account. Here's why.
scenes.on_screen: Gross pay, take-home pay and deductions

scenes.heading: Gross pay vs. take-home pay
scenes.narration: Gross pay is what you earn before anything comes out. Take-home pay, also called net pay, is what's left after deductions. That's the money that actually reaches you.
scenes.on_screen:
Gross pay: what you earn
Take-home pay: what reaches you

scenes.heading: An example pay stub
scenes.narration: Here's an example pay stub with made-up round numbers. Gross pay is $2,000. Federal income tax takes $170. Social Security and Medicare take $153. Health insurance is $90, and $80 goes to retirement savings. Many states also take state income tax.
scenes.on_screen:
Federal income tax: $170
Social Security and Medicare: $153
Health insurance: $90
Retirement savings: $80

scenes.heading: $2,000 earned, $1,507 to spend
scenes.narration: Add it up, and $493 comes out. So $2,000 of gross pay becomes $1,507 of take-home pay. That's about three quarters of the gross amount.

chart.note: Example pay stub with made-up round numbers. Your deductions depend on your pay, your state and your benefits.

scenes.heading: Plan with take-home pay
scenes.narration: That's why a budget starts with take-home pay, not gross pay. You can only spend or save the money that reaches you. And check each stub, because deductions can change, like when you join a health plan.
scenes.on_screen:
Budget the money that reaches you
Check each pay stub for changes

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.narration: Quick recap. Gross pay is what you earn. Take-home pay is what lands in your account. Income tax, Social Security and Medicare come out first, and benefits like health insurance can too.
scenes.on_screen:
Gross pay is what you earn
Take-home pay is what you get
Taxes and benefits come out first

scenes.heading: Quick check

scenes.narration: Now find your last pay stub. In your Money Map, enter your gross pay, your take-home pay and your three biggest deductions.
